messages:
Dave: heads up — since ~03:02 PT we're seeing a large class of traces that only contain ingress and egress spans. internal service spans are missing for a subset of requests.
Emma: ugh. any recent router or sampling tweaks? :thinking_face:
Ben: pushed a small router header-normalization change last night (canary) — removed passthrough of unknown headers in the edge.
Dave: that might be it. traces look correlated to requests that go through the canary pool. here's a quick grep from the trace index: ingress->service-A->service-B (normally) vs ingress->service-B (now).
Carla: can someone paste an example traceparent/otlp headers from a bad request? want to check propagation bits.
Ben: sample trace header we captured: `traceparent: 00-4bf92f3577b34da6a3ce929d0e0e4736-00f067aa0ba902b7-01` and we also use `x-rt-trace` for internal routing. canary was stripping unknown `x-*` by design.
Maya: if the router strips `x-rt-trace` then services will create new roots — that'll explain missing child spans. did we change header whitelist TTL or strip policy?
Ben: yes, the change was to canonicalize headers and drop `x-` prefixes we don't recognize. It was meant to reduce header size. :confused:
Emma: can we repro locally by sending a request with `x-rt-trace` through canary? I'll try a curl.
Emma: ```
curl -v -H "traceparent: 00-11111111111111111111111111111111-2222222222222222-01" \
  -H "x-rt-trace: foo=bar;span=abc" https://canary.edge.redwood/api/echo
```
Maya: if the header is gone on the backend tcp level that's a router problem. if it arrives but collector ignores it then it's Otel ingestion. check collector logs for header parsing errors.
otel-collector-bot: [INFO] 2026-03-18T03:05:10Z exporter/http: failed to export 42 spans: 429 Too Many Requests (backoff applied)
Dave: interesting — we also saw a small spike in exporter 429s around the same time. could be twofold: header stripping + exporter backpressure leading to partial flushes.
Carla: quick dashboard snapshot: traces/sec from service-A dropped from ~120/s to ~18/s for the canary region at 03:02. error rate on exporter up 0.5%.
Ben: rolling back the header canonicalization on canary now. starting canary rollback (will take ~2m).
Emma: after rollback I'll replay a few requests with `x-rt-trace` and confirm internal spans show up.
Ben: rollback done. canary pool updated.
Maya: replayed 10 requests — confirmed `x-rt-trace` persists to service-A and child spans appear in traces.
Dave: nice. still want to investigate why exporter returned 429s. otel bot shows backoff; maybe we hit a burst policy in the gateway. Carla can you pull exporter metrics (queue_depth, send_err)?
Carla: grabbing now — queue_depth peaked at 4500, configured max_queue=5000, export_batch_size doubled for a short spike, send_err mostly 429s to our ingestion endpoint.
Emma: could the header stripping have changed payload size pattern causing different batching? odd but possible.
Maya: separate follow-up: add a unit/integration test ensuring `x-rt-trace` survives the router canonicalization path. and add a dashboard alert for span completeness (ingress->internal->egress %).
Ben: agree. I'll open an RFC to change the router whitelist behavior to allow specific `x-rt-*` headers and add a canary metric.
Dave: action items: Ben — RFC + router test (owner). Maya — add span-completeness alert and a simple replay test (owner). Carla — dig into exporter throttling root cause and whether ingestion returned 429 due to rate-limit or auth blips (owner). Emma — postmortem note and timeline. I'll ping infra if exporter persists to throttle.
Carla: quick note — exporter 429s correlate with a short spike of uncompressed payloads from a batch job at 03:01. seems unrelated but amplified the burst. filing a ticket.
Emma: thanks team. follow-up sync in #eng-platform in 30m to confirm metric changes and PRs. :thumbsup:
